outline: Venn diagrams (up to 3 sets) & word problems

modules.title: Module 1 · Basic Ideas & Notation
modules.html:
A set is a well-defined collection of distinct objects called its elements. We use capital letters for sets: $A,B,U$ etc.

  • $x\in A$: '$x$ belongs to $A$'.
  • $x\notin A$: '$x$ does not belong to $A$'.
  • $\emptyset$ or $\{\}$: the empty set.
  • $U$: the universal set.
  • $n(A)$: the number of elements in $A$.

Types: finite, infinite, equal, equivalent, subset ($A\subseteq B$), proper subset ($A\subset B$), power set.

Key points

  • $n(A\cup B) = n(A) + n(B) - n(A\cap B) = 22+12-5 = 29$.
  • $n(A\cup B) = n(A) + n(B) - n(A\cap B) = 13+16-3 = 26$.

Worked example

Q: If $n(A)=22$, $n(B)=12$ and $n(A\cap B)=5$, find $n(A\cup B)$.
A: 29

Q: If $n(A)=13$, $n(B)=16$ and $n(A\cap B)=3$, find $n(A\cup B)$.
A: 26

modules.title: Module 2 · Union, Intersection, Complement
modules.html:
$A\cup B$ is the set of elements in $A$ or $B$ (or both). $A\cap B$ is the set of elements in both. $A'$ (or $A^c$) is the complement of $A$ w.r.t. $U$: elements in $U$ not in $A$.

$$n(A\cup B) = n(A) + n(B) - n(A\cap B)$$

Key points

  • Union = all distinct elements from either set.
  • Intersection = elements common to both.

Worked example

Q: If $A = \{a,b\}$ and $B = \{b,c\}$, find $A \cup B$.
A: \{a, b, c\}

Q: If $A = \{1,2,3\}$ and $B = \{2,3,4\}$, find $A \cap B$.
A: \{2, 3\}

modules.title: Module 3 · Venn Diagrams & Word Problems
modules.html:
For three overlapping sets:

$$n(A\cup B\cup C)=n(A)+n(B)+n(C)-n(A\cap B)-n(A\cap C)-n(B\cap C)+n(A\cap B\cap C)$$

Word-problem strategy: draw the Venn diagram, start with the innermost region ($A\cap B\cap C$), then move outward, filling each region using the given data.

Key points

  • $n(A\cup B) = n(A) + n(B) - n(A\cap B) = 22+12-5 = 29$.
  • $n(A\cup B) = n(A) + n(B) - n(A\cap B) = 13+16-3 = 26$.

Worked example

Q: If $n(A)=22$, $n(B)=12$ and $n(A\cap B)=5$, find $n(A\cup B)$.
A: 29

Q: If $n(A)=13$, $n(B)=16$ and $n(A\cap B)=3$, find $n(A\cup B)$.
A: 26

More key points

  • In how many ways can the letters of the word 'PENCIL' be arranged — 720.

examples.q: In a class of 40, 22 like Maths, 18 like English, 8 like both. How many like neither?
examples.a: Like at least one: $22+18-8=32$. Like neither: $40-32=8$.

modules.title: Definitions, notation, types of sets
modules.html:
Definitions, notation, types of sets is a key part of Sets (SSS 1, Mathematics). Master the meaning, the main points and how it is tested in JAMB and WAEC questions on this topic.

Key points

  • We use capital letters for sets: $A,B,U$ etc.
  • Types: finite, infinite, equal, equivalent, subset ($A\subseteq B$), proper subset ($A\subset B$), power set.
  • For three overlapping sets: $$n(A\cup B\cup C)=n(A)+n(B)+n(C)-n(A\cap B)-n(A\cap C)-n(B\cap C)+n(A\cap B\cap C)$$ Word-problem strategy: draw the Venn diagram, start with the innermost region ($A\cap B\cap C$), then move outward, filling each region using the given data.
  • A set with $n$ elements has $2^n$ subsets. Here $2^{4} = 16$.
  • A set with $n$ elements has $2^n$ subsets. Here $2^{3} = 8$.

Worked example

Q: If $A \subseteq B$ and $B \subseteq A$, then...
A: A = B — Mutual inclusion means the two sets are equal.

examples.a: A = B — Mutual inclusion means the two sets are equal.

modules.title: Revision and exam focus
modules.html:
Revise the whole topic by working through its key points in order, then test yourself with the 50-question quiz for this topic. Pay attention to definitions, differences between similar terms, and questions that ask you to apply the topic rather than only recall it.

Worked examples

Q: If $n(A)=22$, $n(B)=12$ and $n(A\cap B)=5$, find $n(A\cup B)$.
A: 29 — $n(A\cup B) = n(A) + n(B) - n(A\cap B) = 22+12-5 = 29$.

Q: If $n(A)=13$, $n(B)=16$ and $n(A\cap B)=3$, find $n(A\cup B)$.
A: 26 — $n(A\cup B) = n(A) + n(B) - n(A\cap B) = 13+16-3 = 26$.

Q: If $n(A)=23$, $n(B)=17$ and $n(A\cap B)=6$, find $n(A\cup B)$.
A: 34 — $n(A\cup B) = n(A) + n(B) - n(A\cap B) = 23+17-6 = 34$.

How many subsets does a set of $4$ elements have?
quiz.solution: A set with $n$ elements has $2^n$ subsets. Here $2^{4} = 16$.

quiz.q: How many subsets does a set of $3$ elements have?
quiz.solution: A set with $n$ elements has $2^n$ subsets. Here $2^{3} = 8$.

quiz.q: How many subsets does a set of $5$ elements have?
quiz.solution: A set with $n$ elements has $2^n$ subsets. Here $2^{5} = 32$.

quiz.q: If $A = \{a,b\}$ and $B = \{b,c\}$, find $A \cup B$.
quiz.solution: Union = all distinct elements from either set.

quiz.q: If $A \subseteq B$ and $B \subseteq A$, then...
quiz.solution: Mutual inclusion means the two sets are equal.

quiz.q: The set of all elements in $U$ not in $A$ is called...
Which symbol denotes the empty set?
quiz.solution: The empty set contains no elements; it is denoted $\emptyset$ or $\{\}$.

quiz.q: In how many ways can the letters of the word 'PENCIL' be arranged?
Find the determinant of the matrix $\begin{pmatrix} 3 & 2 \\ 4 & 5 \end{pmatrix}$.
If the determinant of $\begin{pmatrix} x & 3 \\ 2 & x \end{pmatrix}$ is -5, find the positive value of $x$.
quiz.solution: Determinant = $x^2 - 6$. So, $x^2 - 6 = -5 \implies x^2 = 1$. The positive value is $x = 1$.

quiz.q: A binary operation is defined by $x * y = x^2 + y$. Evaluate $3 * 4$.
Simplify $(x+2)^2 - x^2$.
quiz.solution: Expand the square: $x^2 + 4x + 4 - x^2$. The $x^2$ terms cancel out, leaving $4x + 4$.

quiz.q: Which of these shapes is defined by the region $x \geq 0, y \geq 0, x+y \leq 4$?
quiz.solution: The boundaries $x=0$ (y-axis), $y=0$ (x-axis), and the line $x+y=4$ enclose a right-angled triangle in the first quadrant.

quiz.q: For what values of $x$ is the fraction $\frac{x+2}{x^2 - 4}$ undefined?
quiz.solution: A fraction is undefined when its denominator is zero. $x^2 - 4 = 0 \implies x^2 = 4 \implies x = \pm 2$.

quiz.q: Solve for x: $\sqrt{2x + 1} = 3$.
quiz.solution: Square both sides: $2x + 1 = 9$. Subtract 1: $2x = 8$. Divide by 2: $x = 4$.

quiz.q: Solve for x: $2^x = \frac{1}{8}$.
quiz.solution: Express $\frac{1}{8}$ as a power of 2: $\frac{1}{2^3} = 2^{-3}$. Therefore, $2^x = 2^{-3}$, giving $x = -3$.

quiz.q: If $\sin \theta = \frac{3}{5}$ and $\theta$ is acute, find $\cos \theta$.
quiz.solution: Using a right-angled triangle, Opp=3, Hyp=5. By Pythagoras, Adj = $\sqrt{5^2 - 3^2} = 4$. So, $\cos \theta = \frac{Adj}{Hyp} = \frac{4}{5}$.

quiz.q: In triangle ABC, $a=5$, $\sin A = 0.5$, and $\sin B = 0.8$. Find $b$.
quiz.solution: Using the Sine Rule: $\frac{a}{\sin A} = \frac{b}{\sin B}$. $\frac{5}{0.5} = \frac{b}{0.8} \implies 10 = \frac{b}{0.8} \implies b = 10(0.8) = 8$.
